questions.q: Why does a plain FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue break down for a shared training cluster like solara-train?
options: FIFO queues cannot be implemented in software
Jobs vary wildly in size and urgency, so pure submission order can make a high-priority run wait days behind an already-running lower-priority job
FIFO only works with exactly two jobs at a time
Kubernetes does not support queues of any kind
questions.explain: Submission order alone ignores urgency and size differences — a lower-priority job submitted first could block a critical run for days, which is why real schedulers layer priority and fairness on top of FIFO.

questions.q: In a Volcano Queue spec, what is the difference between weight and capability?
options: weight is a hard GPU cap; capability is the relative share when queues compete
weight sets the relative share of the cluster a queue gets when multiple queues compete; capability sets an absolute cap on resources a queue can ever use
They are two names for the same setting
weight only applies to CPU jobs; capability only applies to GPU jobs
questions.explain: weight determines proportional share during contention (e.g., a weight of 2 vs 1 gets roughly double the share), while capability is an absolute ceiling that prevents one queue from consuming the entire cluster regardless of weight.

questions.q: How does Slurm's scheduler typically decide which queued job to run next, rather than strictly first-in-first-out?
options: It always runs the smallest job first regardless of anything else
Backfill logic picks the highest-priority job that fits the currently free nodes, where priority is influenced by QOS and wait time
It runs jobs in alphabetical order by job name
It requires manual approval for every single job
questions.explain: Slurm jobs accumulate a priority score (influenced by QOS and other factors), and backfill scheduling picks the highest-priority job that can actually fit the nodes currently available.

questions.q: What is the key difference between priority and preemption in a scheduling queue?
options: They are the same mechanism with different names
Priority only affects which waiting job starts next; preemption can stop an already-running lower-priority job to reclaim its resources
Priority applies only to Slurm; preemption applies only to Kubernetes
Preemption only ever applies to debug jobs, never to anything else
questions.explain: Priority influences queue order for jobs that haven't started yet. Preemption is a stronger action: it actively interrupts a job that is already running.

questions.q: Why does Solara AI's policy allow debug jobs to be preempted but never preempt a production training run?
options: Production runs are technically impossible to preempt
Killing a running multi-node training job mid-step loses any progress since the last checkpoint, which is a much bigger loss than delaying a short debug job
Debug jobs always run on different hardware so preemption is irrelevant to them
Production jobs are always submitted with QOS=debug
questions.explain: Preempting a long-running production job discards un-checkpointed progress on potentially dozens of nodes, which is almost never worth the capacity freed up — so Solara reserves preemption for low-cost debug jobs only.
